Senses.Explanation: Literally, "go along with it." In the named Dasui case, a monk asks whether "this" is destroyed when the world is destroyed by the kalpa fire. Dasui answers, "destroyed." The monk asks, "then it goes along with it?" and Dasui answers, "go along with it." Later collections repeatedly set this answer beside Longji's contrary "not destroyed" and preserve it as the case's answer-line. Elsewhere the same ordinary phrase can mean following a person or thing; the fixed Chan deployment is its repeated use for Dasui's answer.
Senses.Note: 209 occurrences in 87 allowlisted texts. The master's name has two written forms, "Dasui" (大隋) and the homophonous "Dasui" (大隨); the answer varies between "go along with it" (隨他去) and "go along with it, go along with it" (隨他隨他去). These are transmission variants, not separate senses.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧遂問刼火洞然大千俱壞未審此箇性壞不壞師云壞進云恁麼則隨他去也師云隨他隨他去也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The early record gives the complete exchange and repeats the answer: "go along with it, go along with it."

Senses.PreferredTarget: fixed phrase: following the waves, chasing the swells
Senses.Explanation: The graphs mean “follow or go along with” (隨), “waves” (波), “chase or pursue” (逐), and “swells” (浪): "following the waves, chasing the swells." As a technical Chan term it names (隨波逐浪句), the third of the three phrases (三句) that (德山緣密) (Deshan Yuanming), an heir of (雲門文偃), states in his (上堂): (我有三句語示汝諸人)：(一句函葢乾坤)，(一句截斷眾流)，(一句隨波逐浪)。(作麼生辯)？ The three are handled as a fixed set (函蓋乾坤 · 截斷眾流 · 隨波逐浪) and recur as a stock test-question across the lamp records — (如何是隨波逐浪句)？ — answered with a turning phrase (隨；闊；春生夏長；船子下揚州). The texts pair (隨波逐浪) with (截斷眾流): on a raised (趙州) case a master says (一人隨波逐浪)，(一人截斷眾流), and an (上堂) handles the two phrases together: (看風使帆)，(正是隨波逐浪)。(截斷眾流)，(未免依前滲漏). The corpus assigns the phrase no gloss beyond this deployment, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: The three-phrase formulation is (德山緣密)'s own (上堂); do not attribute it to (雲門文偃) himself — (緣密) is his heir and the corpus states the set in (緣密)'s section (in X81n1568 under the header 雲門偃禪師法嗣). The (上堂) is carried in six allowlist texts — five in (緣密)'s section (X68n1319, X80n1565, X81n1568, X81n1571, X85n1593), while X64n1260 (列祖提綱錄) carries it in the topical (五參提綱) anthology, attributed inline (德山密禪師上堂) (X85n1593 writes 函蓋乾坤, the others 函葢/圅葢). The (如何是隨波逐浪句) test-question is likewise witnessed across ≥2 independent texts. Cross-ref (截斷眾流), (函蓋乾坤). Sense 2 below is the plain idiom, distinct from this named phrase.

Senses.PreferredTarget: plain idiom: drift with the waves
AlternateTargets: following the waves, chasing the swells
Senses.Explanation: The plain idiom: to go along with the waves and chase the swells. The records speak it of persons: of (一切眾生) — (祇為心塵未脫)，(情量不除)，(見色聞聲)，(隨波逐浪)，(流轉三界) (a 上堂 in 禪宗正脉); as a rebuke — (終日隨波逐浪)、(妄生枝節者哉) (a 小參 in 續燈正統); and autobiographically — (明芳愚懦無知)，(自少隨波逐浪) (五燈全書). This ordinary sense is distinct from the named (隨波逐浪句) of sense 1, though both turn on the same image of moving with the water. The texts attach no gloss beyond the literal image, and neither does this entry.
Senses.Note: Attested as the plain idiom across independent lamp records (禪宗正脉 X85n1593, 續燈正統 X84n1583, 五燈全書 X82n1571). The (看風使帆)，(正是隨波逐浪) line (五燈嚴統) pairs the phrase with (截斷眾流) and is therefore treated under sense 1, not here.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'follow circumstances.' The expression occurs 1,829 times in 308 allowlisted texts. Its subject may be a person, conduct, an event, or a thing's functioning. Records pair it with eating and drinking, going on one's way, passing one's days in a boat, responding to people and things, and being free and unconfined. One paired description is 'follow circumstances, free and unconfined; respond to things and act' (隨緣放曠，應物施為). A biography records the saying, 'In all affairs, follow circumstances; this is a way of ease.' A recurrent exchange asks, 'What is following circumstances as the site of the Way?' (如何是隨緣即道場); Baizhang answers, 'Today the summer session begins' (今日結夏). Another text pairs following circumstances with not losing one's nature, describing change in response to circumstances while the subject is not lost.
Senses.Note: One corpus-wide verbal sense, supported across biographies, recorded exchanges, and assembly addresses. Common paired shapes include 'follow circumstances and proceed of itself' in both word orders (27 hits each), 'follow circumstances in eating and drinking' (13), 'follow circumstances, free and unconfined' (107), and 'in all affairs follow circumstances' (10). The site-of-the-Way question receives the calendar answer 'Today the summer session begins' (今日結夏).

Senses.Explanation: Literally and throughout the sampled corpus, “wherever” or “in every place.” Its Chan value lies chiefly in the predicates whose scope it sets. Linji's record has the fixed line “act as host wherever you are; every place you stand is genuine” (隨處作主，立處皆真). Yuanwu preserves the paired formula “act as host wherever you are; on meeting conditions, they are the source” (隨處作主，遇緣即宗). A teaching-seat address defines the work of a lineage teacher with “wherever he is, he raises the guiding principle; he answers questions according to the occasion” (隨處提綱，應機問答). Other records use the same distributive word in “named wherever [it appears]” (隨處立名), “arise right here and perish wherever” (當處出生，隨處滅盡), and “clear wherever [you are]” (隨處明了). These predicates are distinct; the location word is not. No departure from its ordinary distributive meaning was found, and none is manufactured.
Senses.Note: Keep this constituent distinct from the full fixed entry “act as host wherever you are” (隨處作主), while linking the two entries.

Senses.PreferredTarget: act as host wherever you are
AlternateTargets: make yourself host in every place
Senses.Explanation: Literally, 'wherever the place, act as host.' The expression occurs 136 times in 85 allowed texts. Linji's record gives its best-known continuation twice: 'act as host wherever you are; every place you stand is genuine' (隨處作主，立處皆真). The first occurrence continues, 'circumstances come and cannot turn you around' (境來回換不得); the second says that whatever comes is not to be received. Later records most often pair the phrase with 'on meeting circumstances, it is immediately the source' (遇緣即宗). Yuanwu records variants including 'act as host wherever you are; on meeting circumstances, it is immediately the source' (隨處作主，遇緣即宗) and 'act as host wherever you are; on meeting circumstances, immediately act' (隨處作主，遇緣即行). A later collection reverses the order—'the teaching has no fixed form: on meeting circumstances, it is immediately the source; the Way does not travel in vain: act as host wherever you are' (法無定相，遇緣即宗；道不虗行，隨處作主)—and another places the phrase beside 'establish the source and set up the purport' (建宗立旨). The records deploy it as a direct imperative, a quoted Linji saying, and a predicate within assembly addresses.
Senses.Note: The graph 'host/master' (主) is translated as 'host' in the preferred target because Linji's surrounding record repeatedly distinguishes guest and host (賓主); 'master' is retained as an alternate graph-literal rendering. The unpunctuated full Linji continuation 'act as host wherever you are; every place you stand is genuine' (隨處作主立處皆真) occurs twice in the Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies. The phrase later circulates across houses with the circumstance/source pairing and is therefore corpus-wide rather than Linji-specific.
